items.stem: What does WebApplicationFactory<TEntryPoint> provide for ASP.NET Core integration tests?

options.text: An in-memory TestServer and an HttpClient that exercises the real request pipeline
options.rationale: Correct: it bootstraps the app in-memory and hands you an HttpClient against the real pipeline.

options.text: A mocking library that replaces all classes automatically
options.rationale: It does not auto-mock classes; it hosts the app for testing.
It is a test host, not production infrastructure.

options.text: A replacement for the application Program entry point
options.rationale: TEntryPoint usually IS Program; the factory uses it rather than replacing it.

items.explanation: Correct: it bootstraps the app in-memory and hands you an HttpClient against the real pipeline.

items.stem: You are writing integration tests that must not call a real external payment provider. Select TWO sound practices.

options.text: Register a test double for the provider via ConfigureTestServices
options.rationale: Correct: replacing the service with a test double isolates the test from the external call.

options.text: Seed and reset test data so tests do not depend on each other order
options.rationale: Correct: independent, seeded data keeps tests deterministic.

options.text: Call the live payment API with production credentials
options.rationale: Hitting the live provider makes tests slow, flaky and unsafe.

options.text: Share one mutable static record across all tests
options.rationale: Shared mutable state causes order-dependent, brittle tests.

options.text: Hard-code a sleep to wait for the external system
options.rationale: Arbitrary sleeps are flaky and still depend on the external system.

items.explanation: Correct: replacing the service with a test double isolates the test from the external call.

items.stem: What problem does consumer-driven contract testing primarily address?

options.text: Detecting when a producer change would break an existing consumer expectation
options.rationale: Correct: contracts capture consumer expectations so producer changes that break them fail early.

options.text: Measuring the CPU performance of a service
options.rationale: Contract testing is about compatibility, not performance measurement.

options.text: Replacing the need for any unit tests
options.rationale: Contracts complement rather than replace unit tests.
Contracts verify shape and expectations, not transport encryption.

items.explanation: Correct: contracts capture consumer expectations so producer changes that break them fail early.
